entries.entry: SME ERP planning phase completed under CoreSentinel governance. Bound the empty project to the Core first (ADR-003 prevents fact leakage), then inspected 36 sibling Laravel projects and ran 3 read-only specialist deep-dives (SMEOS architecture, SaaS-OMS order engine, commission/attribution across dzi-holistik + AgentStockit + SAAS-Agent). Key discovery: CoreSentinel held ZERO domain knowledge (8 recall queries, 0 hits; empty pattern library) because Phase-8 persistence was never run for the prior ERP-adjacent projects. Prior art supplies ~60 percent of the kernel (tenancy, money, state machines, isolation testing, CI guards) and supplies a catalogue of 10 verified commission anti-patterns including two live duplicate-payment defects. Wrote Planning.md (1420 lines, 45 sections). Deliberately did NOT record the 12 proposed ADRs to the decision ledger - approval is a human act, and recording a proposal as a decision is the exact failure 55-self-evolution.md separates approve from apply to prevent.

P0 Foundation gate CLOSED. Laravel 12.66 + PostgreSQL 16.14 (port 5433, server version probed not assumed - the PG14 client binary on PATH would have misled exactly as it misled SMEOS ADR-005) + Redis + Inertia/React 19/TS/Bootstrap 5. Company tenancy kernel fails closed. 143 Pest tests, PHPStan level 6 clean, Pint clean, tsc strict clean, vite build clean. Three planted violations proved the guards are not tautologies - and the FIRST planting exposed a real defect in my own guard (Pest not->toContain with a message argument passes unconditionally), which is the recorded anti-pattern I had loaded and still reproduced. Also self-inflicted: a line-based comment stripper corrupted 12 PHP files by mishandling single-line docblocks; caught by a php -l sweep and fully restored. Found and recorded INC-0001: coresentinel verify reports a false FAIL on every Pest project because it probes only vendor/bin/phpunit. DataScope resolver deliberately deferred to P1; P0 delivered the tenancy axis only.

P1 Access gate CLOSED. ScopeResolver + Scopeable contract + AppliesDataScope deliver the own/team/branch/company/all axis, fail-closed on every unresolvable path. BasePolicy calls the same resolver as list queries so record access and list access cannot diverge - that shared path is the actual guarantee, not the individual checks. AuditLog is the P1 proving ground: company-scoped, Scopeable on actor and branch, append-only at model AND database trigger. Two real defects found: (1) Laravel's middleware priority() REPLACES the default list rather than merging, which silently put ResolveCompany ahead of Authenticate and made a guest 401 instead of redirect; (2) the append-only DELETE trigger blocked the cascade from companies, making a company with audit rows undeletable - the PDPA collision the plan predicted, resolved with an explicit purge flag. Data scope proven at BOTH the query layer and the HTTP layer, the latter asserting another user's record id appears nowhere in the response body. Three planted violations confirmed the guards are not tautologies. 177 tests, PHPStan level 6, Pint, tsc all clean.

P2 Master Data gate CLOSED. 21 new tables (customers, suppliers, catalogue, pricing, document sequences) bringing the schema to 44 tables with company_id NOT NULL everywhere and 28 composite FKs. PriceResolver returns a decomposition naming every source it considered and why it did or did not match - the winner alone was never the deliverable. Promotions apply on top of the resolved base rather than as another first-match step, a deliberate deviation from the plan's flat list. DocumentNumberService proven with 8 real OS processes allocating 80 numbers; removing lockForUpdate reproduces duplicates on 3 of 3 runs, so the concurrency test genuinely contends. Three defects found: a Postgres column DEFAULT does not populate an in-memory model (fixed with $attributes on 14 models), Laravel pluralised UnitOfMeasure to a table that did not exist (now guarded permanently by a model-to-table existence test), and Larastan types decimal casts as float when they are strings at runtime (probed, not assumed). 436 tests.

P3 Orders gate CLOSED. Three independent status axes (payment/fulfilment/exception) with each enum owning allowedNext() and OrderStateMachine owning the cross-axis rules. Both situations a single status column cannot express are now tested: a COD order packed while unpaid, and an order shipped then refunded. reasonAgainst() returns a merchant-readable sentence, and canTransition/availableTransitions derive from it so the UI, the API error and the guard share one source of truth. Deliberately did NOT inherit OMS defect P1-25 - the machine refuses Paid while paid_amount is short, so status can never contradict money. Order lines freeze unit_cost and the full price_basis decomposition at sale, which is exactly the input ADR-009 margin commission will consume, making Q-18 (is the client's landed cost real) the highest-value open question. Gate proven twice by mutation: planting a status write outside the machine fails the grep guard, and removing the optimistic lock fails the 6-process race on 3 of 3 runs. 502 tests.

P4 Inventory and Purchasing gate CLOSED. All three criteria met and each proven by mutation: SUM(movements) == on_hand asserted per stock line across mixed operations and a full order lifecycle; the last unit sells to exactly 1 of 8 concurrent processes and oversells on 3 of 3 runs when the row lock is removed; the three-way match reports every discrepancy and blocks payment with a readable reason. Deliberately avoided both OMS reservation defects - commit and release each take their own lock (H-02) and reservations are iterated in id order for a single deterministic lock order (H-03). Closed the two gaps carried out of P3: stock now reserves on allocation via an OrderStatusChanged domain event so Orders never reaches into Inventory directly, and product tax applies per line for inclusive and exclusive rates. Approval engine routes by amount bands stored as data rows, refuses self-approval, and keeps an append-only trail. Found a real Laravel defect: the framework auto-discovers app/Listeners, so my additional manual Event::listen registered it twice and every allocation reserved stock TWICE - it presented as reservation logic rather than wiring. Guarded by a listener-count test. 777 tests, 69 tables.

P5 Attribution gate CLOSED. All twelve questions from the plan are answered by methods named after them, each tested: customer origin, order origin, lead generator, closer, revenue by campaign/marketer/salesperson/branch, channel conversion, ROAS, cost per lead, and team target attainment. ADR-008 behaviour proven: first touch wins for credit while every touch is retained, a converted customer inherits its lead first touch, and the order attribution is FROZEN because commission is paid on it. Unattributed is a valid first-class state, never defaulted to a convenient marketer. Caught a tenant-isolation hole before it shipped - DB::table() bypasses the Eloquent global scope, so all twelve reports would have summed revenue across every company; scoped explicitly with 16 filters and guarded by an architecture test. Honest note: three planted violations did NOT fail the leak test because the scoping is layered on both attributions and orders; only stripping the entire layer made it fail, which is redundant protection rather than a weak test but had to be verified rather than assumed. Also hit a real Postgres constraint - FOR UPDATE is not allowed with aggregate functions - so the touch sequencer locks the last row instead. 972 tests, 85 tables.

P6 Commission gate CLOSED. All four criteria met and each proven by mutation: re-run is idempotent (removing the engine check now raises a UniqueConstraintViolationException rather than duplicating), reversal produces a contra entry with negated amount AND negated sources so the trail nets to zero, every commission renders its full deduction breakdown from persisted data rather than prose, and a provisional accrual is barred from payable by both the state machine and a database CHECK. Nine of the ten anti-patterns catalogued from dzi-holistik, AgentStockit and SAAS-Agent are closed; the tenth (payout posting to the ledger) waits on Finance in P7. Found a real Postgres trap: a UNIQUE index does not fire when a participating column is NULL, so the idempotency constraint silently permitted unlimited duplicates for exactly the order-level accruals it existed to protect - fixed with UNIQUE NULLS NOT DISTINCT. Stated the Q-18 assumption on the record: this engine is only as correct as unit_cost, and P4-4 (no landed-cost allocation) is still open, so R-14 is now live rather than theoretical. 1094 tests, 94 tables.

P7 Finance gate CLOSED. Invoice/payment/outstanding reconciles to the cent (3180 = 1260 + 1920, difference asserted as exactly 0.0000) and the four ageing buckets match a fixture with a settled invoice correctly dropping out. The journal is a real double-entry ledger, not a cash book with a ledger-shaped name: balance is enforced by the service, by a CHECK on the entry and by a per-line CHECK, journal_lines reject UPDATE and DELETE at the database so corrections must be reversing entries, and trialBalance() is asserted zero after issue, payment, void and payout. CA-10 is closed - the last of the ten prior-art anti-patterns - with commission posting Dr Expense/Cr Payable on payable and Dr Payable/Cr Bank on payout, clearing the payable account to zero. The payout also flips every commission to paid, which is precisely the AgentStockit double-payment defect (CA-5); both proven by planted violation. P3-2 also closed: invoices now exist and snapshot money at issue. 1212 tests, 103 tables. Q-18 and P4-4 remain open - the ledger is exact but the cost figures flowing into it are still unvalidated.

P8 Reporting gate CLOSED. Both criteria met and proven by mutation. The precomputed rollup is verified against an INDEPENDENT live oracle - rollup by SQL GROUP BY, oracle by PHP iteration with exact Money arithmetic - so the comparison is a genuine cross-check rather than a tautology; planting a cost-times-quantity bug fails it on the first run. Rebuilds are idempotent across three runs and a cancelled order drops out. Every dashboard figure passes through the data-scope resolver: two salespeople see 1000 and 500 while the owner sees 1500, a salesperson with no orders sees zero rather than someone else's numbers, and removing visibleTo fails the test. Breakdown tables use the same scoped query so a chart cannot leak what a list would not. Also closed part of the UI gap I flagged at the end of P7: the first real working surface is a role-aware dashboard with five variants that falls back rather than serving a variant the role lacks. Two P0 tests asserted placeholder dashboard props; one was updated and the other, which was proving company isolation through branchCount, had its intent preserved by asserting branch isolation directly rather than being deleted. 1261 tests, 106 tables.

P9 Hardening: gate PARTIALLY met, marked [~] not [✔]. The gate requires an EXTERNAL security review, which by definition I cannot perform - so I did an internal review against 40-security-protocol.md and converted it into a permanent 19-assertion suite instead, and said plainly that half the gate is unmet. Three real findings: Laravel ships the local disk with serve=>true which registers GET and PUT /storage/{path} with NO middleware at all (unauthenticated read AND write against the private business-document disk), Horizon had no explicit gate so access depended on APP_ENV, and the root path answered every HTTP verb. All fixed and guarded. PDPA erasure implemented - anonymises operational PII everywhere it was written while retaining invoices under accounting obligation, refuses without a stated reason, records itself in the audit trail. The restore rehearsal immediately earned its place: the FIRST backup attempt failed because pg_dump refuses a newer server (client 14.18 vs server 16.14) - the third time the client-versus-server distinction has caused a defect here. Round-trip verified to preserve 106 tables, 11 triggers, 91 checks, 270 FKs, and the restored database still refuses journal edits when probed with real rows rather than empty tables. Also caught a measurement error in my own N+1 test: comparing a cold request to a warm one measured cache priming, not N+1. 1283 tests.
